items.check: All M-001 acceptance criteria are met by traktor_nml/tracklist.py as implemented

3-line tracklist parses correctly; blank and '#' comment lines skipped; hyphen-without-spaces inside title survives intact; leading/trailing whitespace stripped from both halves; a line with an empty half after stripping is unparseable, not a record with an empty field
A line with no spaced-hyphen delimiter lands in the unparseable list carrying its correct 1-based line number and raw text, and does not appear in the parsed list
A line matching exactly one collection entry resolves matched with that entry's primary key; a line matching two entries resolves ambiguous, not matched; a line matching none resolves unmatched
Resolution output order equals input line order, verified on a tracklist whose middle line is unmatched
Two identical tracklist lines resolve independently rather than collapsing onto one result
All M-002 acceptance criteria are met by buildplaylist.py, playlists.py additions, and commands/build_playlist_cmd.py as implemented
build-playlist appears in the top-level help subcommand list with cli.py left unedited (discovered via commands/ package iteration)

New PLAYLIST holds one ENTRY per input line in input order; ENTRIES attribute equals assembled count; each PRIMARYKEY KEY equals the matched collection entry's real primary key (never derived from input text); a name containing '&' and '"' round-trips through re-parseable XML with the name intact

A base already holding a playlist of the requested name yields the numbered-suffix variant, the pre-existing playlist keeps its own name/UUID, and two runs over one base produce different PLAYLIST UUID values
Output document re-parses and every byte outside the receiving SUBNODES span matches the base exactly (prefix/suffix comparison, not substring/count checks)

A tracklist holding one unmatched line, no override, exits non-zero, writes the unresolved report, leaves output path absent; the same run with --allow-unmatched exits zero and writes a playlist of only resolved lines with matching ENTRIES

An --output or --unresolved-report path resolving to the base path, tracklist path, or (for report) output path is refused before any write, via the same bespoke set-membership check as splice_cmd.py (DL-033)

Named target folder absent aborts with no output; named target folder matching >1 FOLDER aborts target_folder_ambiguous naming the count (never first-match-in-document-order); named target folder present receives the node with root SUBNODES COUNT unchanged
A dry run prints stats and leaves the output path absent
A malformed base reports xml_parse_error naming the path and exits 2; a missing tracklist reports input_not_found naming the path and exits 2

An empty tracklist, an all-unparseable tracklist, and an all-unmatched tracklist under --allow-unmatched each abort with a dedicated no_entries_resolved error and write nothing, rather than writing an ENTRIES=0 PLAYLIST
Two tracklist lines naming the same collection track produce two independent ENTRY/PRIMARYKEY elements referencing it, in input order, not deduplicated

A base document with no PLAYLISTS section, root FOLDER, or SUBNODES element at all aborts with a no_root_subnodes error and writes nothing (verified this is genuinely reached via a non-empty/matchable tracklist, not masked by an earlier unmatched-line abort -- see qa-017)

Unresolved report is written as CSV via csv.DictWriter with a header row, newline="" and UTF-8 encoding (matching splice_cmd.py's _write_conflict_report convention, DL-034); parses back with csv.DictReader with header matching printed fields

A non-UTF-8 tracklist file reports tracklist_decode_error naming the path and exits 2 rather than raising an unguarded traceback; a UTF-8-BOM-prefixed tracklist's first line's artist is free of the BOM character
Output commit path calls rewrite.write_bytes_atomically and never writes to the output path by any other means (C-003) -- verified via mock/monkeypatch assertion, not just resulting file content

No occurrence of pyacoustid, chromaprint, fpcalc, an HTTP client import, or CSV/M3U tracklist parsing in these three files; matching.py and confidence.py are byte-identical to pre-existing contents (C-007)

Calling assemble_output directly on input producing unresolved_tracks or no_entries_resolved never creates/truncates/touches the intended output path -- the output path is only opened by _handle_build_playlist after assemble_output returns non-None (C-008)

Confirm whether the plan's manual-Traktor-import validation gate (R-006) has been performed/tracked anywhere (e.g. a manual test-list entry); flag as unautomatable by the test suite itself and note status rather than fail on it
Implementation matches stated behavior: pure text handling, no filesystem/XML involvement, splits on first ' - ' occurrence per DL-031
EntryRecord built with entry=None, source_path=None, empty identity fields and empty LocationParts, confining record_keys to artist_title tier per DL-026

build_new_indexes called once over collection; match_records called once per line with shared indexes; matched record read back via mapping.get("") not a line-derived key; matching.py/confidence.py called, never edited or subclassed
Fragment assembled as ElementTree elements and returned via ET.tostring (not hand-formatted strings); sits beside import_playlists sharing naming/UUID policy

Requested name returned when free; otherwise first free numbered-suffix variant starting at 2, added to in-use set; import_playlists' own collision handling reads through this same function (no duplicate logic)

Behavior text claims 'Validate that every key in the synthesized fragment is a primary key of a base collection record before returning' -- verify whether actual code performs a runtime check or only documents the invariant via comment (known gap); assess per R-010 whether omission is justified (structurally unfalsifiable) or a genuine behavior-text/implementation mismatch worth flagging
Result record populates unresolved_rows on every run including clean ones, not only on failure
Subparser registers positional args (base, tracklist, output) and options (name, target-folder, allow-unmatched, unresolved-report, dry-run) with no --match-confidence flag exposed
Handler wiring matches stated behavior: calls assemble_output, applies path-collision refusal, commits via write_bytes_atomically only after a non-None result

Zero-write-on-ambiguity/error invariant (C-002) holds across every abort path in buildplaylist.py and build_playlist_cmd.py: unresolved_tracks, no_entries_resolved, no_root_subnodes, target_folder_not_found/ambiguous, path-collision refusal, xml_parse_error, input_not_found, tracklist_decode_error
Atomic commit discipline: every successful build-playlist write path goes through rewrite.write_bytes_atomically (temp file + os.replace), consistent with existing write commands
matching.py and confidence.py are byte-identical to pre-existing contents; no new code anywhere reaches into private helpers or reimplements cascade logic (scope creep check, C-001/C-007)
Exit code 2 used uniformly across all build-playlist failure classes (input errors and unresolved-track/zero-resolved aborts alike), matching splice_cmd.py's own precedent (DL-035)
CSV unresolved-report conformance (dialect, header, encoding, newline handling) is consistent across every code path that writes it (abort path and allow-unmatched partial-success path alike)

Verify the M-002 implementer's fixture fix (non-empty/matchable collection so the tracklist line doesn't get rejected as unmatched before reaching the no_root_subnodes check) actually makes the test exercise no_root_subnodes as claimed, and that no other test was left with a similar masked-precondition bug

DL-024 layering respected: core resolution/synthesis/assembly logic lives in buildplaylist.py, commands/build_playlist_cmd.py holds only CLI surface (arg parsing + thin dispatch); check for god-function violations (>50 lines or >3 nesting) in assemble_output or _handle_build_playlist
synthesize_playlist_node/available_playlist_name reuse the same collision-rename+UUID-regeneration machinery as import_playlists rather than duplicating it (DUPLICATE_LOGIC check)

Locate exactly where tracklist_decode_error and BOM-stripping are implemented (not named in any code_intent) and confirm it's a deliberate, tested code path rather than an accidental side effect of a library default
Target-folder resolution walks the full PLAYLISTS tree via SpanIndex/parsed tree (not document-position first-match) so a genuine name collision across branches is caught as target_folder_ambiguous
No dead code (e.g. an unreachable invalid_primary_key branch per R-010's own reasoning) or invalid/unmarked intent markers in the new/modified code
